title: Consent and prompt windows
owns: app/main/remote/prompt-window.ts, app/renderer/prompt/**, app/main/targets/consent.ts, the consent/prompt window creation in windows.ts (small hunk)

findings.title: First-use consent cards sit in a fixed 440x300 window and show only about half their text; 'Connect' / 'Turn on' works after 0.9 s without reading
findings.scenario: The SSH card ('Bring Ember to build-01?') is about 360 px of text in a 198 px scrolling body: it shows through the helper-size paragraph. 'Your voice and your GitHub sign-in stay on this computer', what it reads on the screen there, and 'build-01 keeps its own record' are below the fold. The commands card is 426 px in 198 px, so the part about output going to Copilot, the privacy-related rules and the stop chord are hidden. Only a thin scrollbar (classic scrollbars on Linux; overlay scrollbars hide it on macOS and often on Windows 11) hints at more. The window is not resizable and nothing resizes it. Unlike the command card, the Yes button is not gated on the whole text having been seen.
findings.evidence: Rendered dist/app/renderer/prompt at 440x300 with the real cards from consentText/sshConsent: body scrollHeight vs clientHeight was 364/198 (SSH card with jump host and key), 346/198 (machine changed), 426/198 (commands card with podman and root lines). Screenshots show the cut-off. windows.ts has width 440, height 300, resizable false, and prompt-window.ts never calls setBounds. pressResult/promptView set the consent Yes button to armed:true (a 900 ms delay) only.
findings.fix: Size the prompt window to the card (consent cards about 520-560 px high, capped to the work area), or switch to a larger consent layout. Also keep 'Connect'/'Turn on' disabled until the body has been scrolled to its end, as the command card does ('Read the whole command to allow it'), or add a visible 'Scroll to read all' fade.

findings.title: First-use consent cards are 2 screens of text in a fixed 440x300 window; the stop chord and the 'what it can reach' lines are below the fold, and yes needs no scroll
findings.scenario: A user turning on commands or SSH sees the first paragraph and a scrollbar. Body heights vs the 198 px viewport: 294 px (commands), 356 px (SSH), 382 px (commands in WSL as admin). The stop chord, 'What a command already changed stays changed', the Windows-reach and administrator lines and, for SSH, 'Your voice and your GitHub sign-in stay on this computer' are all below the fold, yet 'Turn on' and 'Connect' are always clickable after 900 ms. The command card forces 'read all'; the consent card, which authorises installing software on another computer, does not. The window isn't resizable.
findings.evidence: prompt1.mjs for linux/win32/darwin: scrollHeight vs clientHeight printed per card (294/198, 356/198, 382/198); shots/P-linux-consent-ssh.png, P-linux-consent-cmd-wsl.png.
findings.fix: Size the prompt window to the card (up to the work area) or make it resizable with a larger default for consent cards (about 440x460). Put the stop chord and the 'what it can touch' line first; enable the yes button only after the body has been scrolled to the end, as for commands.

findings.title: Prompt window (SSH password, passphrase, host key, consent card) is never given the keyboard on macOS and Windows
findings.scenario: macOS: the user asks by the hotkey or ask box (a non-activating panel, so their own app stays active) "on build-01 run df". Ember needs the SSH password, so reveal() runs `w.show(); w.moveTop(); w.focus()` on the prompt window. Ember is not the active app, so the card appears on top without becoming the key window. The user types the password and it goes into whatever app is frontmost (Slack, Mail), in plain text. The card also lacks `acceptFirstMouse`, so the first click on Allow or Connect only activates Ember and is swallowed. Windows: the same when the task was started by voice or an earlier hotkey and Ember has not received input recently, because SetForegroundWindow is refused by the foreground lock and the window only flashes. The prompt page only calls `field.focus()` in the DOM and never checks that the OS window has the keyboard.
findings.evidence: Read end to end: createPromptWindowController takes only {create, ipc, log, os}; `os` is never used for focus, and reveal() just calls show/moveTop/focus. Every other Ember window that takes the keyboard uses the platform hooks: bringToFront (main.ts:274-283) calls sys.lifecycle.focusOwnApp() and inputRef.activate(); the quit question (main.ts:472) and the startup error box call focusOwnApp(); the ask box's takeFocus (main.ts:716-717) does the same. platform/types.ts:469-478 states the rule: "Before one of Ember's own normal windows takes the keyboard ... focusOwnApp", and for win32 "activateOwnWithInput ... (foreground rules)". main.ts comments also say a hotkey does not activate Ember on macOS. createPromptWindow (windows.ts:72-96) is an ordinary window, not a panel, and has no acceptFirstMouse. Could not run on a real Mac or PC; the conclusion follows from Ember's own documented platform rules and Electron's documented focus() behaviour.
findings.fix: Give createPromptWindowController an `activate(win)` callback that main wires exactly like bringToFront: sys.lifecycle.focusOwnApp(), then inputRef.activate(ownId(win)) and focusInput where activateOwnWithInput is true. After showing, check win.isFocused() and, when it is not, say so on the card and in a notification so nobody types a secret blind. Add `acceptFirstMouse: true` to the macOS prompt window.

findings.title: Ember's own approval windows (command card, consent card) are not kept clear of Ember's question bubble, character or task cards, which are drawn above them
findings.scenario: A command question puts 'May I run a command? ... Show the command / Not now' in the bubble; Ember stops where it is (by the cursor, often mid-screen) and the bubble stays until answered. The command window (760x480, created with no x/y, so centred on the primary display) and the prompt/consent window (440x300, centred) open at the same place. The overlay is at 'screen-saver' level and re-raises itself every 2 s, while those windows are 'floating'. So the bubble, Ember's body (which also takes clicks while it asks) and the task cards are painted over the card the user must read in full before allowing, and can cover its text or its Allow / Not now buttons. The user cannot move the bubble; they have to drag the command window away. docs L11 only covers 'another always-on-top window', not Ember's own overlay covering its own approval surface every time.
findings.evidence: Code: the only 'avoid' rect main sends is the settings window (main.ts:316-321 stepAside); windows.ts createCommandWindow/createPromptWindow have no placement; commands/window.ts:224-231 reveal uses setAlwaysOnTop(true,'floating') + moveTop once; overlay.ts:298 and :331-336 keep the overlay at 'screen-saver' and moveTop every 2 s; CommandWindow.cardReady (window.ts:429) checks only visible/focused and the card being scrolled into view, not occlusion. Rendered the question bubble parked at (747,503) over a centred 760x480 mock command window: bubble and Ember sit on the card area (s12-command-window.png).
findings.fix: Treat the command and prompt windows like the settings window: add their bounds (while a card/consent is up) to state.avoid so the bubble keeps off them, and make Ember's follower/park step beside them (stepAside). Alternatively open those windows beside Ember's parked position, or hide the question bubble's body while the panel is open and show a one-line chip instead.

findings.title: Cancel on the connecting bubble (or Forget, or the stop chord) leaves the first-use consent card on screen; its 'Connect' then does nothing
findings.scenario: 'Connecting to build-01… [Cancel]' is on screen while the 'Bring Ember to build-01?' card waits. The user clicks the bubble's Cancel, or presses the stop chord. The card stays up with no hint that it's void, and answering it silently ends with 'Cancelled.' (nothing saved, no feedback).
findings.evidence: Rig: pending card via pw.ask; bubbleAction('conn:build-02:cancel') gave pw.dismiss calls 0 and hideConsent 0; the later yes returned {ok:false,message:'Cancelled.'} and the host consent stayed {version:0}. askCard never wires the abort signal to promptWindow.dismiss.
findings.fix: Pass the connection's AbortSignal to askCard and call promptWindow.dismiss(card.id) when it aborts (Cancel, Forget, stopAll).

findings.title: Cancelling a password or passphrase card is reported as an error: 'Can't connect to build-01 — Connection cancelled' with 'Try again'
findings.scenario: The user clicks Cancel (or presses Esc) on 'Sign in to build-01'. The connection ends and an error-mood bubble titled 'Can't connect to build-01' says 'Connection cancelled' with Try again. Declining the consent card or the bubble's Cancel are silent ('Not now'), so the same intent gets an error style here.
findings.evidence: attempt() sets cancelledByUser when answer.ok is false; failureOf returns {kind:'cancelled', message:'Connection cancelled', retry:true}; runtime fail() then shows the error bubble.
findings.fix: Treat a user-cancelled card like Cancel: hide the connecting bubble and return {ok:false, message:'Cancelled.'}; show no error bubble.

findings.title: The SSH consent card is generic where it should be specific, and a repeat card doesn't say what changed
findings.scenario: The card is built before the probe, so it always says 'unpacked… in ~/.local/share/ember-remote', even for a Mac that gets '~/Library/Application Support/Ember Remote/'. It always says 'On build-01's screen it reads and uses apps only when…' even for a server with no desktop. When ssh -G now resolves the name to a different user, hostname or port, the same card appears ('Bring Ember to build-01?') with the new details in the first line but no 'Your SSH settings now send build-01 to X (was Y)'. Only a changed machine gets a warning line.
findings.evidence: consent.ts sshConsent hard-codes the install dir and the screen sentence and adds a warning only when facts.machineChanged. sshNeedsConsent (line ~159) returns true on resolution change without passing a reason. Rendered cards show identical wording.
findings.fix: Add 'the folder for its system' wording ('~/.local/share/ember-remote on Linux, ~/Library/… on a Mac') or a 'Mac' variant. Pass a changedFrom fact so a repeat card leads with 'Your SSH settings now send build-01 to deploy@new.example.com:22 (before: deploy@old.example.com:22).'

findings.title: Prompt window exposes role=dialog on the <main> element, replacing the main landmark
findings.scenario: A screen reader on the SSH password, host-key or consent card finds no main landmark; the dialog still announces its name and description.
findings.evidence: axe-core on every card kind: [minor] aria-allowed-role 'ARIA role dialog is not allowed for given element' on #card (prompt.mjs). Dialog name and description were correct in the Chromium tree.
